skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render Remotion videos, still images, and transparent exports with practical CLI and configuration guidance.
skill.summary: Choose reliable Remotion commands and settings for standard or transparent media exports.
skill.author: remotion-dev

security_audit.summary: All five static alerts are false positives. The command alerts identify Markdown fences, while the network alerts identify links to official Remotion documentation.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 12-14 use triple backticks as a Markdown fence around a fixed Remotion command. They do not execute Ruby or shell input.
The backticks at SKILL.md line 14 close a Markdown code block. There is no executable backtick expression or command interpolation.
SKILL.md lines 20-22 contain a fenced example for a fixed Remotion still command. The backticks only format documentation.
The URL is a plain link to official Remotion render documentation. The skill does not request the URL or transmit data.
The URL is a plain link to official Remotion still documentation. It introduces no automatic network operation or data disclosure.

content.value_statement: Choosing compatible Remotion export settings can be difficult. This skill provides commands and configuration patterns for videos, stills, ProRes, and WebM.
actual_capabilities: Provides the standard Remotion CLI command for rendering a video.
Provides the standard Remotion CLI command for rendering a still image.
Configures transparent ProRes output with PNG frames, alpha pixel format, and the 4444 profile.
Configures transparent WebM output with PNG frames, an alpha pixel format, and VP9.
Shows global Studio settings and composition-level calculateMetadata patterns for transparent exports.
limitations: It does not create Remotion compositions or application code.
It does not run renders, inspect output files, or diagnose runtime failures.
It covers only basic rendering and transparent ProRes or WebM exports.
Users must verify codec support and playback compatibility in their environment.

use_cases.title: Export a Remotion Composition
use_cases.description: Select the basic CLI workflow for producing a video or still from an existing composition.

use_cases.title: Prepare Transparent Editing Assets
use_cases.description: Choose ProRes 4444 settings for alpha video intended for professional editing software.
use_cases.target_user: Motion designers transferring assets into editors

use_cases.title: Deliver Transparent Browser Video
use_cases.description: Choose WebM settings for alpha video intended for compatible browser playback.
use_cases.target_user: Web developers shipping transparent motion graphics

prompt_templates.title: Render a Basic Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the standard Remotion command to render my existing composition named [composition] to [output file].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a routine video export.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Still Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to render a still from my existing Remotion composition named [composition] to [output file].
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a single image from a composition.

prompt_templates.title: Export Transparent ProRes
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend Remotion CLI settings for a transparent ProRes file that I can import into [editing software].
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an alpha video for editing software.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Transparent Export Defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Studio configuration and calculateMetadata settings for transparent [ProRes or WebM] exports in my existing Remotion project.
prompt_templates.scenario: Set advanced global or composition-specific export defaults.

output_examples.input: I need a transparent video for professional editing software.
output_examples.output: Use ProRes with PNG frames, the yuva444p10le pixel format, and the ProRes 4444 profile. Export the result as a MOV file.

output_examples.input: I need a transparent animation for browser playback.
output_examples.output: Use WebM with PNG frames, the yuva420p alpha pixel format, and VP9. Confirm that target browsers support the resulting format.

output_examples.input: I need a poster image from an existing composition.
output_examples.output: Use the Remotion still workflow and specify the composition and output image required by your project.

best_practices: Choose ProRes 4444 for editing workflows and WebM for compatible browser playback.
Use PNG frames and an alpha-capable pixel format when transparency is required.
Restart Remotion Studio after changing global export configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not expect transparency from codecs or pixel formats without alpha support.
Do not apply global configuration when only one composition needs special export defaults.
Do not assume every browser or editing tool supports the selected transparent format.

faq.question: Can this skill render a video for me?
faq.answer: It provides commands and settings, but it does not execute Remotion or produce files.

faq.question: Does it support still images?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies the Remotion still workflow for an existing composition.

faq.question: Which format is suitable for video editing?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends transparent ProRes 4444 for importing into video editing software.

faq.question: Which format is suitable for browsers?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends transparent WebM with an alpha pixel format for compatible browsers.

faq.question: Can settings be applied to one composition?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows composition-level defaults through a calculateMetadata function.

faq.question: Does changing Studio configuration require a restart?
faq.answer: Yes. Restart Remotion Studio after changing the global export settings described by the skill.
